                                                In India, the festive season has started. Diwali is on the 8th of November this year. Last year, it 
was on the 20th of October, and so, some of the festive stocking that happened in September last 
year is happening in October this year. 
 
Even so, demand through the quarter was healthy, and the trade has stocked up well for the 
season. The initial trends in October driven by the festive demand are also seeing good traction.  
 
Gold prices have been high and volatile. The buyers of the natural diamond jewelry are taking a 
little longer to decide. As such, the results of natural jewelry certification grew only 3% in this 
quarter. Lab-grown is not seeing this hesitation at all.  
At our Investor Day in August, we spoke about lab-grown diamonds under three heads: supply, 
retail, and buyer. Let me take you through each one briefly so that we can see what we saw in 
this quarter.  
                                                On supply, large Indian growers are adding reactors and are doubling their capacity in 3 years. 
Supply is at its base and not at its peak. In the quarter, lab-grown loose certification grew 37%, 
signalling a robust supply ramp-up.  
                                                On retail, certification demand is created at the retail end. The certificate costs less than 2% to 
3% of the retail price, and it is the very reason why consumers buy with confidence. 
 
In India, lab-grown chains are opening up stores, and established jewelers have also launched 
their own lab-grown brands. In the United States, more than 50% of all bridals are now lab-
grown, and other markets are likely to follow this trend. Our lab-grown jewelry certification 
grew 47% in this quarter as retailers stock up for the season.  
 
On the buyers, for many families, lab-grown diamond is the very first diamond that they buy. 
With increase in household income, they buy more pieces, bigger stones, and over many years, 
over the coming years, they will move to natural diamonds. We certify natural diamonds, we 
certify lab-grown diamonds, colored stones, and to the same standards.  
It is the IGI certificate that makes the lab-grown diamond a diamond, and it is the same certificate 
that also protects the value of a natural diamond.  
 
Furthermore, last month in Bombay, the Union Home Minister, Shri Amit Shah, asked the 
industry to keep the entire lab-grown diamond chain in Indian hands, from machines to the 
showrooms. He said the lab-grown market could grow many times over its current size. 
 
We welcome this. IGI was the first international laboratory to certify lab-grown diamonds way 
back in 2005. A market of this size needs an independent standard that the whole world will 
accept. That is what IGI provides, and that is the role that we intend to keep.
